target: मेरा फ़ोन चार्ज हो रहा है, थोड़ी देर में कॉल करता हूँ।
english: My phone is charging, I'll call you in a little while.
tip: चार्ज हो रहा है (charge ho raha hai) = 'is getting charged' – हो (ho) for things happening on their own. If YOU charge it, that's चार्ज कर रहा हूँ (charge kar raha hoon).

target: मैं स्टॉप पर बस का इंतज़ार कर रहा हूँ।
english: I'm waiting for the bus at the stop.
tip: You wait OF the bus, not for it: बस का इंतज़ार कर रहा हूँ (bus ka intezaar kar raha hoon = doing the bus's wait). इंतज़ार (intezaar) always takes का.

target: मैं अभी खाना खा रहा हूँ, थोड़ी देर में फ़ोन करता हूँ।
english: I'm eating right now, I'll call in a little while.
tip: फ़ोन करता हूँ (phone karta hoon) looks like 'I call' but means 'I'll call' – the simple present works as a right-away promise in Hindi.

target: क्या आप मेरी हिंदी समझ पा रहे हैं?
english: Can you understand my Hindi?
tip: 'Can you understand' uses पाना: समझ पा रहे हैं (samajh paa rahe hain = managing to understand). पाना (paana) after a verb means 'manage to, succeed in'.

target: तबीयत ठीक है ना? चेहरा उतरा लग रहा है।
english: Are you feeling well? Your face looks drawn.
tip: लग रहा है (lag raha hai) = 'is looking, seeming': चेहरा उतरा लग रहा है (chehra utra lag raha hai) = your face seems drawn. लगना (lagna) covers impressions.

target: तुम्हें ज़्यादा पानी पीना चाहिए।
english: You should drink more water.
tip: 'You should' starts with तुम्हें (tumhein = to you), not तुम – with चाहिए (chahiye), advice points at the person, so they take the to-form.

target: यहाँ फ़ोटो खींचना मना है।
english: Taking photos here is prohibited.
tip: 'Is prohibited' is just मना है (mana hai = is forbidden) after the plain verb: फ़ोटो खींचना मना है – no 'it', no passive, nothing else needed.

target: मोहन को तैरना आता है।
english: Mohan knows how to swim.
tip: Skills come to you in Hindi: तैरना आता है (tairna aata hai = swimming comes) means 'knows how to swim'. Learned abilities use आना (aana = to come), not सकना.

target: तुम्हें सच बोलना चाहिए था।
english: You should have spoken the truth.
tip: 'Should have' just adds था: बोलना चाहिए था (bolna chahiye tha = should have spoken). The past marker sits after चाहिए, nothing else changes.

target: प्रिया तीन भाषाएँ बोल सकती है।
english: Priya can speak three languages.
tip: सक (sak) never stands alone – it glues onto the bare verb: बोल सकती है (bol sakti hai = can speak). English puts 'can' before the verb; Hindi attaches it after.

target: मुझे दो सौ रुपये और चाहिए।
english: I need two hundred rupees more.
tip: और (aur) usually means 'and', but after an amount it means 'more': दो सौ रुपये और (do sau rupaye aur) = two hundred rupees more.

target: मुझे यह काम आज ही ख़त्म करना है।
english: I have to finish this work today itself.
tip: No extra 'have to' word – करना है (karna hai = is to do) alone means must. The -ना (-na) verb form plus है (hai) carries the whole obligation.

target: रांची जाने के लिए कौन सी बस लेनी चाहिए?
english: Which bus should I take to go to Ranchi?
tip: Verb + के लिए (ke liye) means 'in order to': जाना (jaana = to go) shifts to जाने in जाने के लिए (jaane ke liye = in order to go).

target: निखिल को अभी निकलना पड़ेगा।
english: Nikhil will have to leave now.
tip: पड़ेगा (padega) comes from पड़ना (padna = to fall): the duty falls on Nikhil, no choice in it. चाहिए (chahiye) suggests, पड़ना forces.

target: हमें आधा किलो चीनी चाहिए।
english: We need half a kilogram of sugar.
tip: There is no verb 'need' here – चीनी चाहिए (cheeni chahiye) is literally 'sugar is wanted'. Noun + चाहिए = need; a verb before चाहिए means 'should'.

target: तुम्हें अपनी दवा समय पर लेनी चाहिए।
english: You should take your medicine on time.
tip: लेनी (leni), not लेना – the verb before चाहिए matches its object's gender: दवा (dava = medicine) is feminine, so 'to take' becomes लेनी.

target: शायद मोहन कल तक आ सके।
english: Maybe Mohan can come by tomorrow.
tip: After शायद (shayad = maybe), the verb shifts to the maybe-form: आ सके (aa sake), not आ सकता है. Uncertainty changes the verb ending itself.

target: विजय चाहता है कि हम लखनऊ चलें।
english: Vijay wants us to go to Lucknow.
tip: 'Wants us to go' needs a full clause: चाहता है कि (chahta hai ki = wants that) + हम लखनऊ चलें (ham Lakhnau chalen = we go to Lucknow) – never an infinitive like English.

target: मुझसे यह भारी बक्सा नहीं उठ पाएगा।
english: I won't be able to lift this heavy box.
tip: Impossibility is phrased 'from me': मुझसे (mujhse) + नहीं उठ पाएगा (nahin uth paega = won't get lifted) – the failure comes from your side, and the box बक्सा (baksa) is the subject.

target: हमें एसी ठीक करवाना चाहिए।
english: We should get the AC repaired.
tip: करवाना (karvana) = get it done by someone else: एसी ठीक करवाना (AC theek karvana) is having it repaired, not repairing it yourself – that would be करना (karna).

target: क्या मैं इसे पहनकर देख सकता हूँ?
english: Can I try this on?
tip: 'Try on' is wear-and-see: पहनकर देख (pahankar dekh = having worn, see). Hindi tests things by doing the action, then देखना (dekhna = to see).

target: तुम्हें छाता ले जाना चाहिए, बारिश हो सकती है।
english: You should take an umbrella, it might rain.
tip: सकना also covers 'might': बारिश हो सकती है (barish ho sakti hai = rain can happen) means it might rain – possibility, not anyone's ability.

target: ख़ुदा हाफ़िज़, अपना ध्यान रखना।
english: Goodbye (may God protect), take care.
tip: ख़ुदा हाफ़िज़ (khuda haafiz) – literally 'God (is your) protector', a goodbye from Urdu, common in everyday Hindi alongside नमस्ते (namaste).

target: रेखा अपना होमवर्क कर रही है।
english: Rekha is doing her homework.
tip: Rekha is the subject, so 'her' homework is अपना (apna), not उसका (uska) – उसका would mean someone ELSE's homework, not her own.

target: कृपया मुझे अपना पूरा नाम बताइए।
english: Please tell me your full name.
tip: In commands 'your' is अपना too: अपना पूरा नाम बताइए (apna poora naam bataiye) = tell your full name – the doer is 'you', so अपना points back at you.

target: वरुण ने अपना खाना ख़ुद बनाया।
english: Varun cooked his own food himself.
tip: अपना खाना ख़ुद बनाया (apna khaana khud banaya) – two self-words: अपना = his own (the food), ख़ुद = himself (did the cooking).

target: पधारिए, ये आपका अपना घर है।
english: Please come in, this is your own home.
tip: आपका अपना घर (aapka apna ghar) – अपना stacked after आपका means 'your very own'. A warm host formula: this house is yours too, not just ours.

target: सब अपनी-अपनी जगह बैठ जाओ।
english: Everyone sit down in your own places.
tip: अपनी-अपनी जगह (apni-apni jagah) – doubling अपना spreads it over everyone: each to their OWN place. Hindi repeats a word to mean each/respective.

target: लक्ष्मी ने अपनी माँ को ख़त लिखा।
english: Lakshmi wrote a letter to her mother.
tip: अपनी माँ (apni maa) – अपना (apna) matches the thing owned, not the owner: माँ (maa) is feminine, so it's अपनी whether Lakshmi or her brother writes.

target: मुझे अपने देश की बहुत याद आती है।
english: I miss my country a lot.
tip: You don't miss things in Hindi – the memory comes to you: मुझे (mujhe = to me) + याद आती है (yaad aati hai = memory comes) = I miss my country.
